frontier.hypothesis: A legitimate (non-FAKE-family) C spelling can deny loop.c the two constant hoists, at which point the clean reference-faithful form — not the 8 — becomes the match candidate.
frontier.mechanism: Priced exactly by this session's ALLOCDBG: suppress those two movables and the clean form gets target's $s0/$s1/$s2/$s3 map with four callee-saves at 90 insns, with no other change. The gate is loop.c:695 — a movable is skipped only when all three of (A) `! maybe_never && ! loop_reg_used_before_p`, (B) `! REG_USERVAR_P && ! REG_LOOP_TEST_P`, (C) `reg_in_basic_block_p` are false. (B) is unconditionally true for a compiler temp holding a literal, which is why every clean spelling hoists; session 3 showed a NAMED local plus maybe_never works for 0x1000000 but not for 0x3C0000.
frontier.next_probe: The untried half of (A) is `loop_reg_used_before_p`, not `maybe_never`: a named local READ earlier in the loop body than the point where it is set makes (A) false regardless of maybe_never, which is exactly the position 0x3C0000 sits in. Re-read tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c:690-712 and :920-940 to confirm the predicate FIRST, then enumerate loop-carried spellings of the timeout limit that read such a local before setting it. Screen with tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s7/score.py and confirm the hoist is gone via ALLOCDBG from s7/idump.sh <tag> (a suppressed hoist shows as 7 rather than 8 allocnos, with tbl_11dc at hardreg=19).

frontier.hypothesis: Declaring D_800A1494 as Sony's `CD_intr` STRUCT (rather than `extern u8` indexed through a u8* local) is what produces target's hoisted base register for Intr — `lbu a0,0(s1)` / `lbu v0,1(s1)` at offsets 0 and 1.
frontier.mechanism: Neither the reference spelling (r0: GCC folds the constant address into each lbu as %hi/%lo) nor an explicit u8 * pointer local (r1, and session 6's whole n-family) reproduces target's base register. Sony's source has ONE object with two member offsets. Note H28 killed the `volatile` QUALIFIER specifically; the STRUCT shape is a separate and untested question.
frontier.next_probe: Out of scope for a single-function grind session: it needs the shared extern declaration changed and both sibling bodies adjusted. Assign a structural/rederive session scoped to all three CD_* siblings at once (saEft01Init, cpu_side_move_dir_4 = CD_sync at ~line 366, CD_ready at ~line 480), declaring `typedef struct { u8 sync, ready, c; } CD_intr; extern CD_intr D_800A1494;` and indexing `D_800A125C[D_800A1494.sync]`.

frontier.hypothesis: The session-3 F7 tail (+1: target fills the `beqz $v0` delay slot with `move v0,zero`, we emit a nop) is now readable, because the DBRDBG trace set that session 3 could not get exists in the instrumented cc1.
frontier.mechanism: reorg's fill_slots_from_thread consumes the analogous block for the FLAG exit in this same function but refuses it for the mask exit. Session 3 shelved this because BB2_DBR_DEBUG produced no output — from the wrong binary (build/cc1). tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 carries the full DBRDBG trace set (thr / thr LOSE / thr WINNER / simp / mtlr), plus BB2_NO_FT_STEAL and BB2_ALLLIVE_LABEL to bisect the behaviour.
frontier.next_probe: `BB2_DBR_DEBUG=1 bash tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s7/idump.sh <tag>` on the candidate and on session 3's w1_goto_exits, then find the `thr LOSE` line for the mask exit and read which resource test rejected the steal.
